- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.37 to -0.50 within 3–5 days), model delays correction — reduce forecast by 3–8% for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently overestimates mean reversion speed — if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, forecast should be 2–3% below historical 30-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate downward trend after negative sentiment — add 1–2% upward bias if sentiment remains negative for >5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.30) over 5+ days, model underestimates upside — add 2–4% to forecast if sentiment remains positive.
- Model often ignores sentiment lag — if sentiment is negative 3–5 days ago, adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to account for delayed reaction.
